extracted.intended_audience: epidemiologists, methodologists, statisticians, researchers and journal editors involved in the conduct and dissemination of observational studies
extracted.subtask_description: Guiding authors and peer reviewers to use the STROBE Statement and its checklists/extensions to strengthen reporting of observational epidemiology studies (cohort, case–control, cross‑sectional) and their abstracts. Includes note that extensions (e.g., STROBE‑ME) and draft abstract checklists exist and are being piloted.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Statement purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: STROBE stands for STrengthening the Reporting of OBservational studies in Epidemiology — an international, collaborative initiative of epidemiologists, methodologists, statisticians, researchers and journal editors with the common aim of strengthening the reporting of observational studies in epidemiology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Statement provides reporting guidance intended for authors and journal editors; it is an internationally developed standard endorsed by a growing number of biomedical journals (link to full list) and has associated resources indexed in PubMed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the STROBE checklist when reporting observational studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should follow the STROBE checklist items when reporting observational studies to ensure complete, transparent reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The website links to the STROBE checklists; these are living resources with updates and extensions. Journals endorse the Statement and may expect submitted manuscripts to adhere to checklist items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include checklist items in abstracts (draft STROBE checklist for abstracts)
rubrics_metrics.description: A draft STROBE checklist of items to be included when reporting observational studies in abstracts is being piloted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The draft checklist for abstracts was being piloted (example: at the ECCMID conference). Authors and conference organizers should consider these items when preparing abstracts; feedback on drafts is solicited as part of piloting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate STROBE extensions (e.g., STROBE‑ME for molecular epidemiology)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicable, use the relevant STROBE extension (for example, STROBE‑ME: STrengthening the Reporting of OBservational studies in Epidemiology: Molecular Epidemiology) to capture domain‑specific reporting items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions are published as part of the STROBE initiative (STROBE‑ME published online 24 October 2011); consult the extension appropriate to the subfield to ensure specialized reporting requirements are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use reporting guidelines during peer review to improve manuscript quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Applying reporting guidelines (such as STROBE) during peer review can affect the quality of final manuscripts submitted to biomedical journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site highlights a new article: 'Effect of using reporting guidelines during peer review on quality of final manuscripts submitted to a biomedical journal: masked randomised trial' — suggesting empirical evidence exists that guideline use during review can change final manuscript quality.
